title: Orchid Bakery — Returns Assistant sprint notes
content:
Quick capture from demo + follow-ups (raw). Do not circulate externally without review.

Call summary (2026-02-19 demo):
- Attendees: Asha (RWI SE), Marcos (RWI SE), Leah (Orchid PM), Priya (Orchid Eng), Sam (Orchid ops)
- Goal: validate returns-assistant MVP flow (customer reports item, bot proposes return label/steps, triage to human if edge).
- Mode: Private deployment behind Orchid VPC — they want KMS + audit logs.

Key requirements surfaced:
1) Latency target: average user-facing RTT < 800ms on text generation path (web checkout chat). Peak concurrency expected 150 qps during promos.
2) Deterministic fallback: when model confidence low OR KV cache miss, system must fall back to a lightweight rule engine (regex + heuristics) before human escalation.
3) Sensitive PII: receipts contain CC last4, order numbers. Data plane must strip CC, and all user messages persisted only in encrypted store; retention 30 days.
4) Catalog sync: product catalog is updated frequently — need fast embedding reindex (incremental) and per-site product vector store.
5) A/B rollout: want canary at 5% then ramp by metric (NPS for returns resolution).

Architecture notes (sketch):
- Private control plane in RWI with connectors into Orchid VPC via private link.
- Serving: dedicated pool (quantized L2) for gen; fallback to smaller distilled variant if cost spike.
- Embeddings: local Milvus instance in their VPC; Redwood provides batched embedding endpoint to seed vectors and upserts.
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated user questions (returns policy common Qs).

Gotchas / Risk points (document these for SOC/Legal):
- On-prem vs VPC: they initially asked for on-prem due to audit but clarified VPC-first. Need to confirm HSM/KMS integration timelines.
- Peak concurrency mismatch: their ops spreadsheet lists 400 concurrent chat sessions. Our earlier capacity calc used 150 qps. Re-run cost/latency sims with 400 and 2x avg sequence length (order history included).
- Embedding drift: catalog changes hourly — naive reindexing will thrash. Recommend incremental upserts + TTL + morning full rebuild. Note tradeoff: search freshness vs vector store CPU.
- Debugging visibility: Orchid ops want token-level cost breakdown and per-request context hashes in logs to reconcile user-reported vs served content (PII redaction required).

Implementation notes / engineering tasks:
- SE-4782: infra template for Orchid VPC connector (assigned Marcos). Estimate: 3 workdays (incl. IAM, SGs).
- Add embedding upsert batch API wrapper (assigned Asha) — include chunking + dedupe logic. Accepts CSV of (sku, name, desc).
- Build rule-engine fallback prototype (Leah + Priya) — simple DSL; integrate as pre-checker to reduce false-positive escalations.
- Logging: ensure request_id + context_hash + model_variant recorded; sensitive fields redacted at ingestion (Priya to confirm redaction regex).
- Canary rollout config in Console: create 5% canary schedule with auto-roll back if user escalation rate > 3%.

Prompt / eval notes (initial):
- Golden set: 120 returns queries from their support logs (sampled). We will run eval suite for: correctness (label created?), hallucination rate, instruction-following (is return approval step present).
- Prompt format: system: "You are Orchid Returns Assistant. Follow these policies: only propose return if eligibility checks pass. If uncertain, ask 2 clarifying q's." Keep templated slots: {order_id}, {sku}, {purchase_date}, {user_msg}.
- Temperature: 0.0 for decision path, 0.6 for customer-facing empathetic messages. Need variant routing in runtime.

Next steps (prioritized):
1) Marcos: VPC connector template + initial capacity re-run (due 2026-02-27).
2) Asha: deliver embedding upsert wrapper + sample toolkit for their CSV -> embedded vectors (due 2026-03-05).
3) Leah/Priya: provide 120 anonymized returns examples and a list of common SKUs (sensitive fields scrubbed) — target 2026-02-24.
4) SE: stand up 1-week pilot sandbox in their VPC (dry-run) with minimal model stack (distilled gen + embeddings) — target 2026-03-10.
5) Legal/Sec sync to confirm KMS/HSM and retention: Leah to loop in Security (target meeting 2026-02-26).

Loose notes / brainstorming (raw):
- Consider shipping an offline “returns-eligibility” microservice (rules + small model) that can be open-sourced for partners; reduces load on main gen pool.
- Could leverage per-customer quantization profile: Orchid is price-sensitive — LLM variant selection by route (promo hours -> smaller model).
- UX: show "why this return was approved" box with the justification tokens (sanitized). Useful for CS reps.

Open questions to resolve on next call:
- Would Orchid accept a managed Milvus (hosted) vs their own instance? Cost + ops tradeoffs to present.
- What is legal's stance on storing order_id in vectors (hashed vs plain)?
- Canary success metrics: define baseline escalation rate and NPS delta threshold for ramp.

Notes to self: keep this doc as single source for quick copy to Confluence after internal alignment. When moving to Confluence, scrub customer-identifying logs and tag PRs.

-- end --
